title: EMST 150 Training in Mild-Moderate OSA
official: Evaluating the Efficacy and Feasibility of Combined Expiratory Muscle Strength Training (EMST 150) and Oropharyngeal Myofunctional Therapy in Patients With Mild-to-Moderate Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
summary: Obstructive Sleep Apnea is a condition in which the upper airway repeatedly becomes blocked during sleep, often due to weakness or collapse of the upper airway throat muscles. The purpose of this study is to evaluate whether combining a handheld breathing device (Expiratory Muscle Strength Training (EMST 150)) with structured, speech-language pathology-Guided mouth and throat exercises can help strengthen the muscles that keep the airway open, reduce snoring, and reduce sleep apnea severity while improving overall sleep quality. Participation in this study will last about 3 months. This includes a 5-week home breathing exercise program, two in-person clinic visits (at the beginning of the study and at Month 3), and two short phone check-ins.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Clinical diagnosis of Mild-to-Moderate OSA (5\<AHI\<30 events/hour)
* Patient willingness and physical capability to perform threshold-based respiratory exercises and daily oral myofunctional exercises.
* Documented failure, intolerance (defined as regular use \< 4 hours/night), or patient refusal of standard therapies, including Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) and surgical interventions.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Severe OSA (AHI\>30 events/hour)
* Active asthma, severe or poorly controlled asthma with low symptom perception, or severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
* Uncontrolled hypertension, defined as resting systolic blood pressure \>160 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure \>100 mmHg at screening, or any change in antihypertensive medication within the past 30 days, or significant cardiovascular disease.
* Recent esophageal surgery, recent abdominal surgery, or presence of an abdominal hernia.
* History of spontaneous pneumothorax, or incomplete recovery/healing following traumatic pneumothorax or rib fracture.
* History of lung transplantation or lung resection.
* Current tracheostomy or unhealed tracheostomy stoma.
* Presence of a cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) drain or active intracranial pressure monitoring.
* Active epistaxis (frequent/severe nosebleeds) or active hemoptysis within the past 30 days.
* Tympanic membrane perforation (ruptured eardrum) or active inner/middle ear pathology.
* Unrelated or uncontrolled gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD).
* Known or suspected pregnancy.
* Active use of CPAP, mandibular advancement device (MAD), or hypoglossal nerve stimulation (HGNS) during the study period.
* Any acute medical condition or clinical situation where generating intrathoracic, intro-abdominal, or intracranial pressure (similar to Valsalva maneuver) is clinically contraindicated.
